chunk_findings.detail: The regression test intended to cover `show`, `list`, `board`, and `next` only actually covers `show`. If `run_cli` returns a failure code for those bad arguments, the test still passes because it does not assert the CLI return code; if it raises, the test fails. chunk_findings.detail: `_own_size` measures `log.shard.stat().st_size`, but `log.shard` is the shard selected by the agent name used to construct the `EventLog`. Two concurrent processes that use the same agent name—including the default `agent=""` passed to `keep_stamped`—append to that same shard. So while process 1 runs a read verb (e.g. `show`), process 2 can append events to the shared shard; process 1 then sees `_own_size(log)` grow from `before` to `after`, and `keep_stamped` calls `waves.restamp`. The read verb therefore writes because a foreign process wrote, violating rule r-read-verbs-read-only and contradicting the change's stated falsifier. The docstring claim that "another agent's writes land in its own shard" is false when both processes share an agent name.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_read_verbs_append_nothing_while_another_agent_writes` has no synchronization between the writer thread and the CLI read verbs. chunk_findings.detail: `keep_stamped` is decorated with `@contextlib.contextmanager` and must yield exactly once, but after determining `on` it yields unconditionally at line 64, then yields a second time either at line 66 (`if not on`) or at line 69 (`with counter as appended`). Consequently, any normal exit from a `with keep_stamped(...)` block resumes the generator into the second yield and `contextlib` raises `RuntimeError: generator didn't stop`, so every wrapped command fails after running its body. The same structure also enters `_own_appends` only after that first yield, meaning the append hook is not installed during the caller's command body and cannot count the caller's own appends.

Since each `EventLog` is its own per-agent shard—this same file states “A shard is keyed by agent name”—the `"probe"` shard contains neither the writer’s events nor any restamp events. chunk_findings.detail: The new hook is installed in the process-wide `APPEND_HOOKS` list and filters only on `wlog.root == root and ev.agent == who`; it carries no command/context/thread identity. If two commands run concurrently in the same process—which the existing `_STAMPING` `contextvars.ContextVar` already accommodates—thread A can run a read verb with the default `agent=""` while thread B appends to `EventLog(repo, "")` on the same repo. Thread B’s append matches A’s hook, so `seen[0]` becomes non-zero and A calls `waves.restamp` after its read. That is the same “someone else wrote” scenario as the acknowledged multi-process bug, still violates `r-read-verbs-read-only`, and leaves the read verb restamping because of another caller’s write in the same process. A command-local or context-local registry, or an invocation-specific token compared in the hook, is needed.

chunk_findings.detail: `keep_stamped` is decorated with `@contextlib.contextmanager` but now yields twice on every normal path: once at the first `yield` and again either in the `if not on` branch or inside `with counter as appended:`. `contextlib.contextmanager` requires exactly one yield; when the wrapped command exits normally, `__exit__` resumes the generator at the first yield, reaches the second yield, and raises `RuntimeError: generator didn't stop`. Thus every successful command wrapped in `keep_stamped` fails on exit, and the restamp logic never runs. The same ordering also means `_own_appends` is entered only after the command block has already executed, so its append hook cannot observe the command’s own appends.

This change bypasses that port and adds a direct real-subprocess dependency.
